headline: South Asia: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike.
- Southern Europe: NATO’s Top Commander Unveils Plan for Victory Against Russia.
- Western Russia: Ukraine struck 12 Russian oil refineries in September, Defence Ministry says.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Powerus unveils fully autonomous drone interceptors.
- Military Times, 3 hours ago: Powerus unveils fully autonomous drone interceptors.
Once a threat is detected, the new Guardian 3 interceptors are immediately launched toward it. They strike using advanced AI and navigational systems.
- Military Times, 8 hours ago: Vector, Nammo expand push to mass-produce armed drones.
Executives from both companies say they’re scaling up production of systems that reflect “the realities of how warfighters will employ them.”
The Caribbean - bottom line: Harris wants early guilty pleas to count in more cases.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Harris wants early guilty pleas to count in more cases.
President of the Advocates’ Association of Jamaica (AAJ), Tamika Harris, is calling for greater recognition of early guilty pleas in Jamaica’s criminal justice system, arguing that they can spare victims further trauma and help reduce court backlogs. “Encouraging early guilty pleas is not about rewarding criminal conduct. It is about promoting accountability, protecting victims and ensuring the timely administration of justice.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Appeal court slashes trespass award in Manchester land row.
THE COURT of Appeal has slashed a $400,000 damages award to $150,000 while upholding a finding of trespass against the Simmonds family in a long-standing Manchester land dispute between neighbouring families. The Morgan family – comprising Marylyn Morgan, her sister Melva Morgan, and her son Jason Salmon – took the Simmonds family to court in 2017, alleging trespass after members of the family began constructing a house on land in Swaby’s Hope, Spur Tree, Manchester, which the Morgans claimed to have possessed and used for over 40 years.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Southern Europe - bottom line: NATO’s Top Commander Unveils Plan for Victory Against Russia.
- Balkan Insight, 3 hours ago: NATO’s Top Commander Unveils Plan for Victory Against Russia.
The strategy draws on lessons from Ukraine, putting cheap drones, AI and rapid military strikes at the heart of NATO's response to any Russian attack.
- Politico Europe, 3 hours ago: EU approves biggest Russia sanctions package since invasion began.
“This is the single largest expansion of our sanctions list since Russia started its war," Kaja Kallas said.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: NATO’s top general lays out plan to fight Russia — with or without America.
Gen. Alexus Grynkewich aims to send a clear signal to the Kremlin that the alliance will resist any attack.
- Politico Europe, 3 hours ago: French supermarkets face food crisis after cyberattack hits refrigerators.
France's cyber agency coordinating with European counterparts in response to hackers.
Western Russia - bottom line: Ukraine struck 12 Russian oil refineries in September, Defence Ministry says.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Ukraine struck 12 Russian oil refineries in September, Defence Ministry says.
Ukraine’s Defence Ministry says the strikes also hit five military-industrial complex facilities, including a drone manufacturer and a plant involved in Kh-59 missile production.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Family with child killed in Russian rocket artillery strike on Cherkaske in Donetsk Oblast.
Three people, including a child, have been killed and four others injured as a result of Russian strikes on the settlement of Cherkaske in Donetsk Oblast on the morning of 12 October.
- The Moscow Times, 6 hours ago: Russia Weighs Drone Defenses for Data Centers After ‘Unprecedented’ Yandex Attacks.
The strikes on Yandex data centers have caused server outages that triggered service disruptions for users.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russians attack Vinnytsia: reports emerge of strike on confectionery factory.
Russia has attacked civilian infrastructure in Vinnytsia. Users on social media suggest a possible hit on a Roshen confectionery factory, but there has been no official confirmation.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Air Strikes Kill Dozens of Gold Miners on Sudan-Egypt Border.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Sudan: Air Strikes Kill Dozens of Gold Miners on Sudan-Egypt Border.
[DW] A Sudan-based rights group said 72 people were killed in a remote, disputed area known for illegal gold mining.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 13 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan Condemns Suicide Drone Attacks On El-Obeid.
[SNA] Khartoum (SUNA) - The Government of the Republic of Sudan strongly condemned the attacks carried out against the city of El-Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan State, on Friday using suicide drones, attributed to the rebel Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia. According to preliminary information, the attacks resulted in civilian injuries and damage to homes and property.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 6 hours ago: Somalia: Somalia's Former Prime Minister Warns of Risks From Military Moves Near Former Leaders' Homes.
[Shabelle] Mogadishu, Somalia -- Former Somali prime minister Hassan Ali Khaire has warned that military movements targeting the homes of former national leaders in Mogadishu could fuel instability and deepen the country's political crisis.
- Africanews, 10 hours ago: Eritrea urges United Nations to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia.
The neighbours have accused each other of starting a war over Tigray, where Ethiopia says Eritrea is backing rebels.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Oil tanker reportedly attacked in Strait of Hormuz region.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Oil tanker reportedly attacked in Strait of Hormuz region.
Plumes of black smoke rise from a Petro Dolphin oil tanker by a drone attack off the coast of Oman.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: One killed, children among 24 injured after unexploded Hezbollah cluster bomb detonates in North.
Northern District police officers and bomb disposal experts responded to the incident, which was declared a mass-casualty event by the IDF.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Iran-Saudi talks on Yemen’s Houthis: What’s in it for Tehran?.
Tehran seeks dialogue in Yemen conflict, warning a military solution risks complicating the volatile regional situation.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: US, UK among 29 countries condemning Iranian hybrid attacks, state-sponsored violence in West.
“Any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce people on our territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable,” the statement read.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: 'Breast Cancer Is Not a Curse' - Ansah's Plea to Women As Cases Soar in Malawi.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Malawi: 'Breast Cancer Is Not a Curse' - Ansah's Plea to Women As Cases Soar in Malawi.
[Nyasa Times] Malawi's First Vice-President, Jane Ansah, has appealed to women to seek medical attention as soon as they detect unusual changes in their breasts, warning that late diagnosis continues to undermine efforts to combat one of the country's most persistent health challenges.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 12 hours ago: Nigeria: Xenophobia - 111 More Distressed Nigerians Return From South Africa.
[Daily Trust] Another batch of 111 distressed Nigerians have returned from South Africa following the xenophobic attacks in the country.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, Africanews, Taipei Times, Al Jazeera - Middle East, just now: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike.
A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, killing one person — a Pakistani resident — and wounding 11 others, a day after another deadly attack claimed by the Yemeni group forced authorities to suspend operations there. Saturday’s attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh has long militarily supported the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: KP's policies will come from Islamabad now, not Kabul, says Kundi.
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Monday that gone were the days when there would be no coordination between the Centre and the province, adding that “our policies will now come from Islamabad, not Kabul”. “Gone are the days when there was no coordination between the Centre and the province. Gone are the days when we used to fight needlessly with another province … We will have coordination with the Centre; our policies will come from Islamabad … not Kabul, Jalalabad or Kahandar. It is clear,” Kundi said at a press conference in Peshawar a day after taking the helm in KP.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Achakzai draws Balochistan parallel as he flays Centre over governor's rule in KP.
National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai on Monday drew a comparison between Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, criticising the government’s move to impose emergency and governor’s rule in the former. The federal government on Sunday imposed emergency in 12 districts of KP, and placed the province under governor’s rule, taking note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: DPM Dar defends emergency and governor's rule in KP, says measures not politically motivated.
A day after the government imposed governor’s rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar defended the move, saying it was not politically motivated but instead taken to curb terrorism. DPM Dar made the comments while addressing a seminar in Islamabad, a day after the federal government imposed emergency under Article 232 and the governor’s rule under Article 234 in KP. The Cabinet recommended the move, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.
Asia - bottom line: US turns to low-cost Blackbeard hypersonic missiles to overwhelm Chinese defences.
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: US turns to low-cost Blackbeard hypersonic missiles to overwhelm Chinese defences.
The US Navy aims to field a relatively low-cost hypersonic missile on its carrier-based fighters, a weapon that could pose a new challenge to the air defences protecting Chinese warships and coastal military installations, experts said. California-based defence company Castelion’s Blackbeard is designed to fly at more than five times the speed of sound and strike ships and land targets. Unlike more expensive hypersonic weapons, it is being developed with an emphasis on affordability and mass...
- Taipei Times, just now: Dozens killed in airstrike on gold mine in Sudan.
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: Israel pupil, 15, killed, over 20 hurt, after suspected leftover bomb detonates.
An Israeli teenager was killed and more than 20 other people injured Monday by a suspected leftover Hezbollah bomb as they hiked near the Lebanese border, officials said. The Israeli military, which dispatched helicopters to the scene, said an initial review showed the explosion was likely caused by an unexploded munition from Lebanese militant group Hezbollah. The explosive, which was likely a cluster bomb from a round of fighting three years ago, went off in the hands of a pupil who picked it...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Dog shelter worker awarded HK$89,000 over canine attack despite volunteer claim.
A Hong Kong court has awarded more than HK$89,000 (US$11,340) to a worker at a dog shelter who was seriously injured in a canine attack, rejecting her employer’s argument that she was a volunteer. District Judge Harold Leong Kwok-on said on Monday that the employment relationship between Kelly Animals Shelter in Lau Fau Shan and the victim had been established despite no contract being signed, noting she was paid, allocated work by staff and did not manage the business or shoulder profits or...
India - bottom line: 4 Pakistani Terrorists Killed In PoK Blast During Infiltration Attempt.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: 4 Pakistani Terrorists Killed In PoK Blast During Infiltration Attempt.
The powerful explosion caused by an improvised explosive device (IED) rocked a forward village along the Line of Control (LoC) in the Krishna Ghati sector of Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch district on Monday.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: The Himalayas are getting a new war machine as Indian Army expands its drone arsenal.
The Indian Army has ordered 225 First-Person View drones aimed at enhancing operational capabilities in Ladakh. These drones will be provided by Gurgaon-based Aerodrone Robotics Pvt Ltd following successful trials at high altitudes. Increasing drone deployment is part of the Army's modernization efforts in response to regional tensions and warfare evolution. The drones are expected to improve surveillance and logistics in challenging terrains.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: On Run For 3 Years, Madhya Pradesh Mass Shooting Accused Caught In Gurugram.
The 37-year-old accused, identified as Ramusingh Dhirasingh Tomar, was traced to a warehouse in the Gopalpur GIDC area of Gurugram, Haryana. Police said he had been evading arrest for over three years by frequently changing identities.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Kerala crash: Old video shows accused teen’s Mini Cooper speeding at 220kmph.
Suhail Sajeev, a 19-year-old, was arrested after a crash in Nedumbassery that killed three people. The victims were returning home on a scooter when a Mini Cooper struck them from behind. Sajeev's Instagram video showed reckless driving, with a speedometer reaching 220kmph prior to the incident. Police suspect he was intoxicated during the accident, with ongoing investigations. Further inquiries into alcohol service by local bars are also being conducted.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Arrest warrant sought for man accused of murdering mother-in-law, kidnapping wife amid annulment suit.
- Yonhap News Agency, 7 hours ago: Arrest warrant sought for man accused of murdering mother-in-law, kidnapping wife amid annulment suit.
SEOUL, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- Police on Monday sought a warrant to arrest a man on ...
- Yonhap News Agency, 15 hours ago: (URGENT) Cheong Wa Dae holds emergency meeting on N.K. missile launches.
(END)

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Australian government says online platforms have ‘responsibility’ to block US military execution live stream.
- The Guardian - Australia, 14 hours ago: Australian government says online platforms have ‘responsibility’ to block US military execution live stream.
Federal government urged to prevent Australians from viewing planned broadcast of Fort Hood mass murderer Nidal Hasan’s execution Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates The federal government says online platforms have a “responsibility” to block a US military execution from Australians, saying “no-one” should see it, amid cross-parliament calls for its broadcast to be restricted.
- ABC News Australia, South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Judge warns jurors as Russell Brand prepares for rape trial in London.
British actor, comedian, and presenter Russell Brand has appeared in a London court for the start of his trial on historical sex offences.
- The Guardian - Australia, 3 hours ago: More part-time bosses and co-CEOs could keep women in leadership and narrow Australia’s pay gap.
Uneven caring responsibilities combined with a lack of flexible work options have prevented women from staying in senior positions, research suggests Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast More part-time bosses and “co-CEOs” could keep women in leadership and narrow Australia’s gender pay gap, the federal government’s Workplace Gender Equality Agency says. WGEA warned resistance to gender equality was growing and urged employers to make management more flexible to reduce the gender pay gap, where women earn $0.79 for every $1 a man makes on average. Continue reading...
- ABC News Australia, 5 hours ago: AI boom could widen income inequality, Labor MP warns.
AI use in the workforce could see the wage gap shrink, while worsening inequality.
